subject_line: Your labs look worse before they look better
opening: Happy Sunday, friends. We've got a big one this week, and honestly the timing couldn't be better. Whether you're three weeks in or three months deep, something in this issue is going to make you feel a lot less alone.

hero.title: What Carnivore Does to Your A1c in 90 Days
hero.teaser: You switched to carnivore, you feel better than you have in years, and then your lab results come back looking somehow worse. Fasting glucose up, A1c not where you expected it. Before you panic and call it a failed experiment, there's a specific reason this happens on a low-carb diet, and it's not what your doctor is probably telling you. Sarah breaks down exactly what's going on inside your blood work at the 30, 60, and 90-day marks. You'll want to read this before your next appointment.
hero.cta: Read before your next lab draw

supporting.title: Hair Shedding on Carnivore: Why Month Three Is Worst
supporting.teaser: Sarah says it's almost always about one specific thing, and fixing it is simpler than you'd expect.

supporting.title: Stalled at Month Three? Here's What to Change
supporting.teaser: The pattern behind month-three stalls is real, and apparently so is the fix.

supporting.title: Hypothyroid on Carnivore: Why the Scale Won't Move
supporting.teaser: If your thyroid is underactive, Sarah says the standard advice might actually be working against you.

try_this_week: Pull out your most recent blood work and write down your fasting glucose and A1c. If you don't have labs yet, schedule them this week. Knowing your baseline before you change anything else is the only way to know if the diet is actually moving the needle for you.
looking_ahead: Next week we're getting into something the community has been asking about for months, and the answer is going to surprise people who think they're already doing carnivore right.
